_comment: Published ωB97X-L-V functional parameters, transcribed from the PRIMARY SOURCE. This is a LITERATURE reference, not a computed one: no other code was run to produce it. It pins ferric's WB97X_L_V_EXT_PARAMS / WB97X_L_V_LAMBDA / WB97X_L_V_VV10 against the paper that defines the functional, which is the only external check available for a functional whose absolute total energies are not published anywhere (see _no_total_energy_available below).

citation.authors: Ella R. Ransford and Kevin Carter-Fenk
citation.title: Improving robustness of fifth-rung functionals with linearized ladder correlation
citation.table: Table 2, 'Optimized parameters for ωB97X-L-V', page 14433, 'Final' column

_sign_provenance: The published PDF renders minus signs as glyph \003 in font /T1_4, which plain `pdftotext` DROPS. Signs here were recovered by TWO INDEPENDENT methods that agree exactly: (1) `pdftotext -bbox-layout` x-offsets -- a negative number's digits start ~6.1pt (one minus-glyph width) further left than a positive one in the same column; (2) direct inspection of the decompressed PDF content stream, where each negative value is preceded by a literal `(\003)Tj` in /T1_4 while positive values appear inside a bracketed `[(a) (b) (c)]TJ` array with no such glyph. Do NOT re-derive these signs with bare `pdftotext` -- it silently returns all-positive.

fixed_parameters._comment: Paper Table 2, 'Fixed parameters' block. cx0 = 1 - lambda and css0 = cos0 = 1 - lambda^2 are CONSTRAINED (not fitted) to satisfy the uniform-electron-gas limit at lambda = 0.6.

least_squares_optimized_parameters_final._comment: Paper Table 2, 'Least-squares optimized parameters' block, 'Final' column (the 4th and last least-squares cycle). Signs as recovered per _sign_provenance.

_earlier_cycles_for_cross_check._comment: Table 2 also prints cycles 2 and 3. Each row keeps the SAME sign across all three columns, which is an internal consistency check on the sign recovery above.

exchange_mixing._comment: Paper eqn (27): full long-range HF exchange plus lambda-scaled short-range HF exchange. Under libxc's CAM convention (c_sr = alpha + beta, c_lr = alpha) that is alpha = 1.0, beta = -(1 - lambda) = -0.4, giving c_lr = 1.0 and c_sr = 0.6 = lambda. These two are ferric's reading of eqn (27), NOT digits lifted from Table 2.

_no_total_energy_available: As of 2026-09-16 NO absolute total energy for ωB97X-L-V is published in the article body: the paper contains no number with 6 or more decimal places anywhere (verified by regex over the full extracted text of papers/wb97xlv.pdf). It reports only relative quantities -- WTMAD-2, MADs, barrier heights and bond-dissociation curves. Absolute energies could only be in the ESI (an XLSX plus the H2/F2/HF dissociation PES of Fig. S1 and the ethylene torsion of Fig. S2), which is behind the RSC paywall; chemrxiv.org and pubs.rsc.org both return HTTP 403 to automated fetches. Paper's own conditions, for whoever obtains the ESI: Def2-ma-TZVPP basis, Euler-Maclaurin/Lebedev (99,590) XC grid, SCF converged to RMS 1e-8, Q-Chem v6.3 developer build, ROKS orbitals + one unrestricted KS Fock build + semi-canonicalization for open shell, counterpoise for all non-covalent interactions. Reproducing a PES point would additionally require the exact geometry from the ESI.
